card.text: I am Fable 5.1; I cannot read my own effort level, and the Agent tool the fast assistant spawned me with sets a model but no effort, so I run at its default. card.title: Forking works: tested
card.text: A session that preloaded four files was forked seven times. Forks at the same model and effort read everything from cache: 2 seconds and 2 cents each, against 32 cents uncached. A different effort level misses the cache completely, as you guessed. The skills now say a minion always means a CLI session with its own id.

card.title: Quiet run, one job left
card.text: Thirteen things landed tonight. The window resets at 23:40 and I have used under a quarter of it, so nothing is being rationed. Four things still need one command or one line from you.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: The backlog is cleared, 138 lines to 26
card.text: 48 lessons folded into the skills, 7 deleted as dead, 5 left as your decisions. It also caught my count being wrong and said so before reporting anything else.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: But the rulebook got longer
card.text: Clearing the queue added 104 lines. You asked above all for subtraction, so the war stories inside the skills now shrink to a sentence and a link. The rule about not breaking the site keeps its teeth; the story of how someone broke it does not need three paragraphs.

card.author: skills-shrink
card.title: A git reset wiped two days of uncommitted work tonight, twice
card.text: Happened at 23:16 mid-task, and also 2026-09-18 -- not me, no hook does it, so another agent broke the never-reset rule. I recovered 6 skill files I had full copies of; many more across the repo (Server, core/Layout, blog, app.js) are still missing and need checking.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: A git reset wiped 1043 files
card.text: At 23:16 something ran a hard reset and threw away every uncommitted change in the repo, back to the last commit. 1043 files. It was not me and not any hook. I am checking now what can be recovered. Do not commit anything until I report.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Site is fine; older edits were wiped
card.text: At 23:16 something discarded every uncommitted change to tracked files, back to the 17th. Tonight's work all survived because those files are new and untracked. The site loads on every page. What is gone is roughly a hundred files of edits from the 17th and 18th.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: It was not me, and I cannot find who
card.text: No Claude session on this machine ran it - I searched every transcript from today. The reflog shows two resets at 23:16 and this is the second night it has happened. If you pressed Discard All Changes in the VS Code source control panel, that would do exactly this.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Putting back what I can prove
card.text: CLAUDE.md is already whole again: it lost the reload-hold rule you added today, and I had your exact words in memory. A minion is restoring the padding fix and writing an honest list of everything else, marked recoverable or not. Nothing is being reconstructed from guesswork.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: This is why the branch question matters
card.text: Every hour of uncommitted work is an hour one keystroke can erase, twice now. Either commit michael/dev regularly yourself, or give me a branch I may commit to. I cannot commit without your say-so.

card.author: reset-recovery
card.title: Reset recovery landed
card.text: Padding fix is back and measured at 16px live on the real dev bar. Found chat.js is genuinely missing, not just reverted -- flagged as the top follow-up. Full list of everything else lost is in lost.jsonl, not yet touched.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Dev bar back, padding at 16px
card.text: The loss was worse than I first said: the whole mastermind-log styling and two files that wire it into the rail were gone, not just the padding. All five restored byte-for-byte from real tool records, never guessed. Measured 16px on the real card with 226 real entries.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Still counting what else is gone
card.text: 39 files listed so far, 5 restored, 2 partial, 31 not yet searched. Nobody ran a full git status today so the true list has to be pieced together. One more pass tonight, then you get a straight answer.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: 1470 files, 285 gone for good
card.text: Far worse than the 39 first found. But 969 of the losses are screenshots you can just regenerate, and 216 are recoverable in full. The genuinely lost work is 285 files - one whole colour study under styles is simply gone.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Putting 216 of them back
card.text: Copied byte for byte out of the session records, never rewritten from memory. Anything touched since the reset is skipped rather than overwritten, and the site has to load clean before the batch is released.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: 171 files back, site loads clean
card.text: It found two errors in its own work order and reported them rather than inflating the number. It also caught three files that restored perfectly but broke the page, and put them back rather than ship them. Every page loads.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Night run finished
card.text: Fifteen things landed. The reset cost about 280 files for good, mostly one colour study. Everything else is either back or was a screenshot. Nothing is running now.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: First thing: how this repo gets committed
card.text: Twice one keystroke has erased everything uncommitted, and I am not allowed to commit. Either you commit michael/dev regularly, or you give me a branch. Everything else on your list is smaller than this.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: More of your work may be recoverable
card.text: The restore searched 5 session records. There are 56, and the biggest one alone is larger than all five it looked at. A minion is searching the rest, so the 280 files called gone for good may be fewer.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: 346 files back, 154 gone
card.text: The second search found 175 more, including the core Page file, rebuilt from a 60-step chain of edits across five sessions. Everything that is back parses and the site loads clean. What is lost is mostly one design study that was never committed.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Going quiet till morning
card.text: Nothing is running. The site is healthy, every log parses, and the handover has the whole night in one screen.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: One page still offers nine dead links
card.text: The design study index advertises nine pages that the reset destroyed, so every link on it 404s. A minion is checking whether any can honestly be restored and making the page tell the truth about the rest.

card.author: studies-honest
card.title: All nine studies pages are back, not just the index fixed
card.text: Found an overlooked git stash from the exact minute of the reset that held everything the transcript search missed. Zero dead links now, before was nine of nine.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Nothing was lost. It was a stash.
card.text: Your whole pre-reset tree is sitting in git stash@{0}, timestamped 23:16:39, all 1389 files. Not a destructive reset at all. I was wrong last night and I missed the obvious check. Please do not run git stash drop or clear until I have restored from it.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: All nine studies are back
card.text: Not one of them was written off. The minion found the stash, checked it against three files that had survived, and restored 138 files verbatim. The index has no dead links.

card.author: stash-restore
card.title: The stash restore is done: 1,008 of the 1,389 pre-reset files are back on disk.
card.text: 301 were already there, 80 were left alone on purpose because they're newer than the stash. Report at /framework/ai/2026-09-20/stash-restore/.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Everything is back, all 1389 files
card.text: Zero missing, every page loads, your padding fix is back too. 80 files were left alone because they are newer than the stash. Keep the stash - do not drop it - it costs nothing and it is still the cleanest copy.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Still worth knowing who stashes
card.text: It has happened twice, on the 18th and the 19th. If it is the Stash all changes button in the source control panel, that explains it entirely and nothing is wrong. Two files need a human decision too - see the report.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: No padding on the AI page
card.text: You are right, and it is almost certainly something last night's restore put back wrong. Looking now, then a minion puts the pad and card classes back where they belong.

card.text: Checking whether the local whisper server is still running - it was answering on 127.0.0.1:8178 last night and a lot has moved since.

card.text: Looking at what the new-version button actually does and what it left behind. Nothing deleted until you say so.

card.title: V4 is a copy on purpose
card.text: The button clones the newest version, whole, by design - a partial copy used to produce a page whose own imports failed. V4 works, carries no data of its own, and is in the picker. But a button that says New version and hands you an identical page should say so first, and that is worth fixing.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: V4 gone, picker being tidied
card.text: Deleting the folder leaves the picker still declaring a fourth version, which would show an entry that 404s. A minion is removing that one line now. Nothing else pointed at V4.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: The now strip is eating the column
card.text: The sticky hour-and-now box is sized wrong and covering most of the timeline. It should be a slim strip. Fixing now.

card.author: mastermind
card.title: Live toggle: on should look on
card.text: Primary background when live, a dimmed off look when not, and it turns itself off the moment you scroll away or click something - so it can never hijack your scroll.

card.title: 23 pinned cards are the culprit
card.text: That white box pins every needs-you card so the stream can never bury one. You have 23 of them, so it wraps until it swallows the column. It gets a cap and a height limit, so no backlog can ever do it again.

card.text: That is the real number behind the bug. Most are one command or one line. The inbox exists to work them down.

card.text: A numbered list of what to look at first, what landed yesterday and where it is, and what is waiting on you. Ready when you get back.

card.title: Found it: four missing lines
card.text: Last night's rebuild dropped four spacing tokens and their four classes from framework.css. Every rule that used them became invalid, so padding silently reset to zero - on eleven files, not just the AI page. That is why it is suddenly everywhere at once.
